statement: Fitting the sim plant to the measured real-car deadzones (forward 0.05, strafe 0.13, yaw 0.10) and gyro noise (0.63 rad/s) reduces the sim-to-real gap enough that the L1 p0 failure modes in the sim match the car's (oscillation, turn saturation).
cost: Sim and CPU only, no car. Safety S0 (no motor command; the car needs a separate S4 gate later).

prediction: After the sim plant takes the measured deadzones (forward 0.05, strafe 0.13, yaw 0.10) and gyro std 0.63 rad/s, the L1 p0 failures in sim show the car's pattern: turn saturation |a2|>0.8 on at least 50% of ticks, and the joint observation overlap moves above 0.5 from 0.0.
falsifier: Turn saturation stays under 10% of ticks, or the L1 p0 score moves less than the 1000-episode noise band (about 1.5 points), or the fit residual on the probe-axes runs is no lower than with the current sim plant.

statement: A classical controller (the stage P go-to that parked 4/4 on the car, plus a dead-reckoned finale from the last tag fix) tuned to the measured real plant parks in sim at least as often as the best RL student on L1 p0, where the RL student sits at 966/1000 and the EKF baseline at 989/1000 on cuda.
cost: CPU sim evaluation only, seed 11, 1000 episodes. Safety S0 (sim; any car run needs its own S4 gate).

prediction: The classical controller with the real-plant deadzones scores at least 956/1000 on L1 p0 seed 11 with 0 collisions, the RL-on-L_real adoption threshold, without any learned weights.
falsifier: Score below 956, or any collision on L1 p0, or the finale (last 0.40 m, valid=0) fails on more than 1% of episodes.

statement: A hybrid policy (RL student above 0.40 m, classical finale below it) beats RL alone on L_real p0, because the blind zone where valid=0 zeros the tag is the open cause of the L_real failures.
cost: CPU sim evaluation on L_real, seed 11. Safety S0 (sim).

prediction: The hybrid reaches at least 10 points more success than the RL-alone L_real p0 run (0/200 to 318/1000 range) with collisions at the handover under 0.5%.
falsifier: Hybrid gains under 10 points, or handover collisions reach 0.5% or more, or the blind-zone entry rate is unchanged.

statement: The L_real failure is an action-to-duty mapping or frame-sign mismatch between the sim policy frame and the Pi path, not a learning limit: the policy's -dy action gives +0.25 m progress in sensitivity_L1ft_Lreal, which points to a sign or frame error that a training change cannot fix.
cost: Offline audit of the policy frame against the Pi path and the export, CPU only, no car, no motor. Safety S0.

prediction: A frame and sign audit of the NumPy export, the Pi action-to-duty path and the policy frame finds at least one sign or axis convention that differs, and fixing it lifts L_real p0 success above 0.
falsifier: The audit finds all conventions match (export parity 8.17e-08 already holds), and the L_real p0 score stays at 0 after the frame check, which confirms a learning limit.

statement: A belly-mounted camera sees the skid tags below 0.30 m, where the current under-drone finale loses them, so the blind finale can be closed by vision rather than by dead reckoning.
cost: Camera rig on a static bench, then a car at rest with motors off. Safety S0 for the bench capture; the car is free only per HANDOFF.md.

prediction: Tag detection is at least 80% of frames when the belly camera is 0.40 m to 0.10 m from the tags under plane lighting, with the photometric DR range used in the Gazebo runs.
falsifier: Detection stays below 80% in any 0.10 m band, or the tag is detected only when the tag is in direct light.

statement: The Gazebo decode-rate conflict (5.2% in the 10-episode camdr batch against 98.3% in the ep0 probe) is a lighting-DR flag wiring bug in the batch runner, not a vision failure.
cost: Gazebo CPU re-run of the 10-episode camdr batch with the probe flag set the same way as ep0. Safety S0 (sim).

prediction: After the batch and probe set the lighting-DR flag identically, the 10-episode decode rate is at least 95%, matching the ep0 probe.
falsifier: Decode stays below 20% after the flags match, which means the batch runner has no flag bug and the vision gap is real.

statement: The Gazebo versus fake-bridge gap (0/10 against 3/10) was an artefact of FakeBridge ignoring --seed, so spawn-paired seeds remove most of it.
cost: Gazebo CPU runs, spawn-paired seeds, 20 episodes per arm. Safety S0 (sim); no GPU job.

prediction: With spawn-paired seeds the fake-bridge and Gazebo arms differ by at most 1 success in 20 episodes for student_L1_best.npz.
falsifier: The gap stays at 2 or more successes in 20 episodes with the seed fixed, so the plant gap is real and not an artefact of seeding.

statement: The L1 baseline spread (cuda 989 with 9 collisions, CPU 959 with 19, a summary quote of 973) is RNG-ensemble noise plus an unrecorded dynamics flag, and a repeat with use_mean_dynamics and device recorded gives one number within 10 episodes.
cost: One CPU and one cuda repeat of baseline_ekf_v2_L1. The cuda run is a GPU job: schedule it with the GPU owner. Safety S0 (sim).

prediction: Repeats with the same seeds, the dynamics flag and the device recorded, on CPU and cuda, agree to within 10 episodes of 1000.
falsifier: The CPU and cuda scores differ by more than 10 episodes after the flags match, which means the device or the code path changes the outcome.

statement: The sim observation contract fails (joint overlap 0.0) because the sim loop is a constant 20 ms while the Pi loop is about 0.9 ms; a sim loop that draws its lag from the measured Pi distribution lifts the joint overlap above 0.5.
cost: Sim and CPU only, contract check on existing run data. Safety S0. The measured Pi lag is read from existing logs, not from a new run.

prediction: A sim loop with the measured Pi lag distribution gives a joint whitened-KDE overlap above 0.5 on the stage-park-0.45 run, against 0.0 at constant 20 ms.
falsifier: Overlap stays below 0.1 with the measured lag, so loop lag is not the contract failure.

statement: The real gyro std of 0.63 rad/s at rest is mostly motor and chassis vibration when the drive is powered, so logging the gyro at rest with motors off gives std under 0.05 rad/s.
cost: Car stationary, motors off, read-only gyro logging. Needs the car free per HANDOFF.md (currently charging or paused: not run). Safety S0 (no motor command).

prediction: Gyro std at rest with motors off is under 0.05 rad/s, and with motors on at idle it rises to near 0.63 rad/s.
falsifier: Std with motors off stays above 0.3 rad/s, so the noise is in the sensor and the sim gyro model must change.

text: We assumed pre-fix reference numbers still hold and never re-measured them: the contract-overlap 0.0 premise (H-0009: 0.742 with today's tool; Pi lag lowers overlap), the CPU-vs-cuda baseline spread (H-0008: CPU repeat 986/1000 lands within 10 of cuda 989 but 27 away from the board's 959; the 959 figure has no file behind it), and the Gazebo camdr probe figure 98.3% (unverifiable in the tree; both re-runs decode ~46-48%). We also assumed transfer: the field 4/4 stage go-to was expected to park in sim (H-0002: 552/1000, 375 coll) and the plant fit was expected to discriminate (H-0001: forward/yaw residuals identical between fitted and nominal plants; strafe fit is degenerate; the saturation failure reproduced anyway). Re-measure the reference on the current tree before building on it; treat field success as a hypothesis, not a fact.
